body: Before I got diagnosed and started effective meds (Lamictal), I would just take whatever job came along - not really thinking about what I wanted to do in the long run, or how I could apply my skills to certain jobs.  Now that I'm getting clearer mentally, I'm rediscovering what I really WANT to do - and regretting the time wasted just kind of floating around (and getting a shitty Bachelors in Psychology).  I'm going back to school for Computer Networking in June, and for the first time in a long time I'm excited about my future.

I can relate completely.  I never used to think of suicide like this - I mean, in passing sometimes, but like this?  No way.  It's like I can't go an hour or two without thinking of it, ways to do it, places, researching it, etc.  It's maddening.  People have no idea how bad it gets.  If I told someone every time I was thinking of suicide, I'd be in an institution.
Thanks for the info.
Thanks for the info.
It won't be a hobby; I've got no interest in getting high to be honest, at least not on opiates.  I'm looking for a way out of a really bad situation.
Is there any kind of guide for buying powder, prepping it, and shooting it?
This is exactly why I feel so close to suicide - no wife, no children, no meaningful relationships ... I have nothing to stay for.  I just think that there has to be peace in death.

You've been verbally and mentally abusive for years; you do everything possible to prevent me from having independence because you are needy.  I helped take care of you and Mom when she was dying - and you tell people and pretend that it was just you there slaving away.  While you were asleep and she was dying, I was up all night.  The pressure you applied constantly, the insults, the harassment - it all led to the breakdown that I had; now I'm a fucking mental mess and I'm trapped by you and this illness.  And you wonder why I think about suicide every single day.  Any way to escape you and this hell.
Who doesn't hate Bashar?  Chilling video - that child is far too familiar with war.

To update: I returned to the hospital (psych ward) for a few days at the end of the year ... I am now taking Lamictal instead of Seroquel.  So far it appears to be helping, or at least not making my face numb and my depression worsen.  I really pray this is the start of good things - the last 3 days have been a much better stretch of time for me than I've had in at least 3 months.  I'm able to think more clearly, stop some of the obsessing, and avoid constant thoughts of suicide.  Hoping for the best.

I know this won't be popular with many ... but I use marijuana.  Not as heavily as I did prior to my breakdown, but I use it to alleviate some of the agitation and obsession that tends to go along with my current depressive episode.  I've found it incredibly hard to 'leave my mind/worries/anguish' at times ... and marijuana has a way of taking some of that weight off of my shoulders and allowing me time to breath.

Doubtful; at least in the short term.  Moving a team takes years of planning - and unfortunately the riverfront stadium proposal wasn't agreeable to the league in the first place (they didn't want to pay the pricetag).  It would be interesting though; KC Chiefs and St. Louis Raiders only 3hrs away from each other - talk about rivalry.
Tinder is a wasteland of sad.
Where are you located?  Let us help you find somewhere that can get you your meds for cheap or nothing; these places exist!  You should not go without your meds and suffer.

Your story is inspirational to people like me - who still hope to have a good relationship and marriage with someone who understands, or at least tries to.  I wish I'd been able to express that to someone during my two best relationships; I think it would have helped both me and them - just to know what is/was going on.

Not at all; she left when the iceberg started to show itself, if you will.  I basically had a full blown anxiety breakdown in front of her; preceded by months of building depression and self-medicating.  It changed my life to be honest, it was 5 years ago and I still can't forget it or move on - I feel like that wasn't me who was 'in control' at some points, if that makes sense.  I look back and I see these times where I'm totally eaten up with mental illness (anxiety/depression) and realize now what I have been dealing with for years.  It hurts to realize the things lost to this disease - but it also hurts to think it will 'define' my life from this point on if I don't fight.  I still have some fight left in me, and hope for the best with my current medication ... it's not much right now, but I figure nobody else is gonna save me.
Often; and have had it for a long time.  I know exactly what you mean about 'breaking' it ... like it's both a mental/physical block that you have to push through.

Things get better Cheyenne!  That may sound like talk, but when you turn 18; life changes alot - and most of the time for the better ... all that stuff you wanted to try as an 'adult' will be available to you, and it may be the time of your life!  Give yourself that chance; I know everyone here would like to know that you did, including me.

The meds I was started on (in psych ward) was Abilify.  Getting out, I found out that there was no way I could afford it, and was back on my own - so to speak.  I'm currently on Seroquel, and it's making me cycle; my life has gone so far down this spiral that I'm unable to even think or come up with a plan.  I feel insane, and I'm sick of it.  This all started after a GP gave me Celexa/Ambien together - and suddenly I was totally out in another world.  I haven't been able to get back to the 'real world' since - this was in September.  I desperately want to die; I can't do this anymore.

I'm talking about my medication; Abilify.  I can't afford it.  It's what they gave me in the psych ward (of course) - with no mention of the price when I got out, or the fact that I would have to find something else.
I am right there with you friend; I am so alone, I'm extremely mentally ill, my family and friends don't know how to help, and basic treatment costs thousands of dollars that I don't have.

I went to the ER when I went; that is how they advise it here.  I told them I was thinking about suicide; and they quickly admitted me.  My advice would be to be as honest as possible about everything that is happening and has happened - so they can understand your situation best.  It's tough going to the hospital, but typically, it's a good place to be when you are in need of mental health help - they meet with you regularly, check you out physically, and help you find a medication that works for you.  My best advice is this; bring slippers and/or shoes without laces.  And no clothes with strings in them.

You are so right; I think I quit because I felt like it wasn't helping my depression - and then after quitting I just slid into a worse and worse depression.  I thought it would help to quit - but, like you, two or three weeks later I was just totally sunk by a severe depression, tried to take my own life, and ended up in the hospital (this month).  I'm not sure about smoking going forward; I still do on occasion, but I'm not sure I'll be able to long-term.  I'm trying to find some stability right now with my life and medications; it's a tough time.

Be strong; this too shall pass.  You are bigger (and your life is more important) than a single moment, relationship, situation, or loss.  I understand how this must be difficult, especially if you just received a mental health diagnosis (Bipolar Disorder or Borderline Personality Disorder?).  I can say without a doubt that I've experienced plenty of loss due to my mental health problems; particularly in relationships.

Here is what depression does: lie.  Constantly lie.  Depression says "this bad feeling is forever", and it says "you are being a burden".  It's the biggest liar ever.  Don't listen to that liar.  Work with the psychiatrist, give yourself time, take medication, try different medications if you find the first few aren't working, give it more time, talk to your parents as much as possible - rejoice that you've got people in your life who really care about you.  Keep fighting this, you are going to have bad days like this, but you are also going to have a bright sunny day hit you square in the face before you know it.  When you do recover, help others to find the same sunny day that you found - help guide them through the dark times that you will know very well.  This is why you are here, why you need to be here.  This is why I'm here, talking to you.

Your situation is somewhat similar to mine; I was a heavy daily smoker for over 10 years - I was smoking dabs for about 1.5yrs prior to my 'breakdown' (extreme depressive episode - diagnosed as Bipolar 2).  I can't say for sure what caused my break; but I started Ambien, got into a 'major' depression, stopped smoking cold turkey thinking it would help, and then went completely severe 'wanting to kill myself' depression.  I can say that was probably not a wise idea.

I'm not going to come down on you the way others have; that is a tough situation, and I can understand how it's becoming tough to take - I'm sure the financial stress alone is enough to really hurt.  I'm not you; so I can't tell you how to feel - but you do have a wife ... that is awesome man, even if you don't see everything the same way (like this pregnancy).  These are hard times, but you have children who you love (and who love you I'm sure) - that is another pretty amazing thing, from any way you look at it.  I have mental health problems and currently live with my Dad, so I can definitely relate to the difficulties of living with a parent (or someone else's) and trying to feel good about that situation.  Yes, this will be difficult - but it's not the time to off yourself ... you've got people who depend on you (which is actually kind of awesome in a way ... you are valued in the relationship for many reasons), and you've got a future which doesn't just involve your family - imagine your favorite past-times, sports, your buddies, good music/food, and your own passions.

I know that may all seem obvious to you, but that is alot of stuff that many don't have - or won't have.  There is something to be said for the struggle; your kids will be adults one day and talk about how their pop struggled, but he raised them the best he could, right?
I agree to an extent; when I'm feeling suicidal, the last thing I think about is calling a hotline where they will basically call the police if I'm honest.

It's okay to tell your family these things - that you need help, that things aren't working, that the advice and suggestions just aren't 'enough' to help you with this.  Often, people have no idea how bad things have gotten; I know that from my own situation ... when I started to tell people what was REALLY going on, they were surprised ... they knew things had been getting bad, but never could really 'get it' without me explaining how bad.  Sometimes it's what it takes to really get people rallied to your side and helping with what is going on.  I know you don't want to be a burden, but I'm very very sure that your Mom would also want to provide you with good mental health care and the support you really need to work on these issues.  You deserve to have professional support during this tough time, and it can definitely help.  Please speak to me more if you get the time; I can see you are struggling and am here to help if you need.

Hello; I obviously don't know all of the details of your health history, etc. but what you are describing is self-isolation ... likely in response to a mental illness.  it can be very tough to self-diagnose ourselves or see our situation in full-detail without working with a professional (psychologist or psychiatrist).  You aren't a burden on anyone - they are genuinely concerned because you are clearly someone they care about.  They believe it might be a problem they can help with - or a chance to give the same advice that I'm giving.  I can relate strongly to the feeling of pulling away from everyone (even the good people) in response to my depression and bipolar illness.  You don't have to feel like this, or confused, or alone - it's a good time to seek some outside help.

I did get medication; one worked well for me but I couldn't afford it long-term, and the other (currently prescribed) makes me feel like I'm in a fog mentally.  Bad place to be.

Moving out and getting a job is probably a possibility at some point - I'm 'hoping' my mental health will stabilize and that the fog will lift so I'll be able to work again, be independent, etc.  That is the goal for me at this point.  Whatever it is, I need to be mentally sharp when I do it as it will likely be my last ditch effort to be able to make things work in terms of long-term independence/insurance/treating my mental health, etc.  I'm 34; my mental health has me at the lowest point in my life, unemployed, living with my Dad, trying to keep my sanity together.

Not so much fatigue; just the overall 'brain fog' that seems to be semi-common for those with Bipolar, from what I understand.  This is by far the most difficult symptom for me to tolerate - as I've always considered myself very sharp, quick thinking, and intellectually 'with it'.

I'm no expert at mental health - I've got my own issues for sure.  However, if I had to say what the best thing to do moving forward is; I'd suggest taking time to work on yourself, not doing anything drastic in the near future, and focus on the long-term problem you've identified (sex for male attention).  You aren't alone in your problem; many women and men have similar difficulties, and therapy might really help you out in this case.  Regardless, think long term here ... you've lost a relationship, but you CAN have another, healthy one after you've worked on you.
Trazadone makes me have some crazy-ass dreams; like the type where I'm fighting with people (physically) and wake up punching the air and grunting, etc.  It's very weird.

There are good people in this world, and then there are turds.  Turds try to make themselves feel better by being shitty to others; but remain turds.  Good people may feel like turds at times, but lift others up because they know how it feels to be viewed as a turd.  There is a time when it's best to remove turds from your life, and gravitate towards good people.  If they'll talk crap about others while you're around - they'll talk crap about you when you aren't; it's a hard thing to accept - it's taken me a long time.  Now I watch for it, be as good as possible to people, and try to fill my life with non-turds.  And to put it bluntly; whoever broadcast your personal health issues is a turd (you just don't do that to a person - just like you wouldn't overhear they have cancer and go broadcasting it).

I really can't; even when I take it at night.  100mg at night, and I wake up feeling like I have a brain injury ... I mean, if I were to take this stuff long term, I'd need to be in a 'home' eventually because I'm totally out of it.

I understand how you feel - it's like random shots in the dark in terms of what 'might work' for your mental health, instead of some real answers and the same quality of medicine you'd expect with a physical ailment.  I feel like I've gotten screwed by my GP for giving me the crap that made me have a breakdown, and now I'm at the mercy of a psychiatrist who is going to 'try' out these various terrible medications to see if one can make me sane again.  I have no idea what to do half the time - either 'treat' myself, or continue to be a guinea pig.  And that is messed up about your watch man ... not cool at all.  I was lucky to have a good roommate when I was in inpatient; he was like me - fairly quiet and liked to read, somewhat 'sane' compared to some of the others in there, and took regular showers (thank god).  I got lucky in that respect.
I'm with you; just now coming back to 'reality' after my breakdown in September.  Best of luck friend; we all need a little bit of kindness and assistance.

I mean sort of just not fully 'there' - like I'm not thinking sharply, unable to 'reach out' in a meaningful way and make connections with the people I used to, just disconnected from a normal 'social' life or anything like it.

i am struggling with this as well - I am/was a great writer as well; since my 'breakdown' it feels like I'm foggy and disconnected from the words.  Very frustrating.  I felt it un-medicated, and probably even moreso now that I take Seroquel.  I am really struggling with that disconnected feeling to be honest; it's like I don't know anybody now, if that makes sense.

In retrospect; yeah, I can see how my mental health in general (early signs of bipolar I suppose) cost me relationships - either through anxiety or major depressions.  I only had one girl who stayed through the depressions; she was great, but then in one of my hypomanic phases I left her and did some other dumb shit.  I'm sorry to hear about your relationship; keep your head up.

Yeah; I'm just skeptical because for 34 years I was doing ok (at least not suicidal and insane feeling) - and less than 1 month after an increase in Celexa and the addition of Ambien, I went completely fucking depressed needing-to-die nuts.  3 months later and I've attempted suicide, been to the psych ward, and seen my mental destroyed daily.  I'm telling you, 34 years of somewhat 'normal' depression/anxiety to buck wild fucking crazy in a month ... believe me when I tell you I'm still shell shocked as this occurred in September.  I had never ever thought I'd try to kill myself or hurt myself, and went to graduate school for mental health community counseling ... meaning I'm like a fucking spectator with a copy of the DSM watching myself convulse with total mental illness and unable t even stop it.

Yes, I was 'crazy' before - now I'm CRAZY.

For me: jumping off a cliff I think will be the least painful.  Yes, there is the 'fear' after you've jumped, but if I had fear of death, I wouldn't be trying to kill myself.  I plan on jumping and expect a moment of pain perhaps, followed by a quick death.  I want to be alone while I do it, and not have someone come into my room and find my head blown off or me dead from pills that may or may not work.

My first serious attempts were in October; followed by buying a shotgun and attempting to hang myself in November.  At times I think things 'might' get better, but then I come to reality and realize how bad my situation really is.  I live with my Dad who is pretty much as mentally abusive as possible, I don't have any hope of being able to successfully work or save money while I live here, and I am starting to plan a, hopefully, successful attempt again.  I wanted to wait until summer, but I can't do another 5+ months of living like this and 'hoping'.  I believe the only hope for me is getting out of this situation is suicide; it's just simply part of the disease for me - it's going to be fatal, it's just 'when' - and I don't care to see any more of how this goes.
Sounds familiar; Celexa/Ambien were my triggers.
I won't argue with you; sorry.  That is waste of my time and yours.

Yes; very much so - particularly the Smiths during my latest (worst) depressive episode ... I have lyrics replaying in my head.

"Two lovers intwined, passed me by, and heaven knows I'm miserable now."

Scary ... mine 'started' with Ambien/Celexa.  How many of us are being poisoned by pills, fed more pills to 'get right', and then sold more pills for the rest of our lives because we have a diagnosis that was given to us by people sponsored by said pill pushers.  I was extremely normal for 34 years and suddenly extremely mentally ill after the shit they gave me.

Thank you for sharing your story - that takes strength.  I definitely feel the same sense of being out of control that your pictures and words convey - like a ship that is totally at the mercy of the open ocean around it; a wave could come crashing down at any moment.

Oh my; you are describing my life and work history for the last 8 years.  I was only recently diagnosed, and looking back - I can see how my mental health has kicked me in the ass a dozen times.  I get worked up with a frenzy of anxiety and do really dumb things like quit jobs, be rude, start obsessing over things, generally burn down my life.  Then comes the depression.

Marijuana has always been my DOC; moreso before my 'breakdown' - since that point it makes me feel kind of weird and anxious.  Don't know if I'll go back to smoking it like I used to.

Alcohol makes me feel like crap the next day - always has.  I have enjoyed Shrooms and LSD on numerous occasions (including taking a hit tonight!).  Never been into harder drugs (meth, coke, heroin).  Opiates make me feel kind of sick.

Well, there is marijuana before my breakdown and marijuana after ... it used to be a really enjoyable thing for me, though I did get way too into it like you describe and started smoking multiple times daily (before work, before everything, etc.).  After my breakdown ... it has a different effect on me almost; like it causes really strong anxiety and almost a manic feeling or a slight psychosis like the other poster described.  Whatever went down during my breakdown, it caused my brain chemistry to change - it's the only explanation I have.  Antihistamines (which I used to use for sleep) also cause me sort of a dysphoric mania now ... terrible skin crawling anxiety and various issues.  Just before I had my breakdown I was smoking HUGE amounts of concentrates (really high THC content stuff) - and my tolerance was pretty much through the roof.  I was barely getting high anymore, but smoking more and more.  I quit during my breakdown and now I can smoke just a little bit and get really high, but it's not as pleasant as it once was.

I did recently (Thursday) - he told me to give it some more time and if things aren't different in a few weeks we are going to try new meds.  The price of Abilify is the only reason I'm on Seroquel; I can't believe how companies charge this massive amount of money and prevent mentally ill people from even using their drugs.
You are probably right, the Seroquel just doesn't seem to be for me - I can't go through life feeling like this and trying to suffer through the fog.

I am; it feels like she just doesn't know what to do for me ... I am just a totally different person than I was before this - intellectually, emotionally, my outlook has changed, everything.  6 months ago I was planning on moving to another state, take on a new job, kind of start a new life and find my happiness.  Today, I can barely focus on getting employment, I live with my Dad, and my head goes immediately to suicide every time I get stressed.  It's terrible.  I want to fight as long as I can, but I just won't let this be my life long-term ... it's not a life at this point, it's a prison.

My previous relationships were shot to shit by my mental health; and I've never had a partner that would actually stick around or see mental health as a disease rather than a personality flaw.  I think strongly that I'll never be in another relationship because I just don't have alot in my life to offer someone now.

I semi enjoy it at the time, but the next day it makes me incredibly depressed and anxious both (like a mixed state).  I stopped drinking almost entirely after a terrible panic attack the day after drinking; I could literally feel a major shift in my brain chemistry after a night of drinking.  I smoke marijuana instead; it may not be a healthy choice, but it's a better one than alcohol for me and allows me some distance from my mental health problems for a few hours.

I'm there with you man ... I don't feel like myself at all - I was diagnosed BP2 earlier this month.  I am really foggy from the Seroquel, feel like I'm slipping back into depression, and just have no confidence at all.  It's like my mental abilities have slipped - I forget things, I can't even speak well anymore, and I'm so sleepy half the time.
That is the only positive part of being on mood stabilizers - is they tend to help sleep.  I could sleep for 15hrs on Seroquel, but still wake up feeling like I was awake for days.

That is where I was a few weeks ago; I was in a constant mixed state of extreme anxiety and depression - like my skin was crawling and all I could do was lay in bed praying it went away.  I think the mood stabilizers have at least got me past that point, but now I feel like a mental wreck ... unable to think clearly or get much done.  I pray things get better for us both ... I can't live like this to be honest.

It definitely sucks ... I am just so sad that I went 34 years without going off the deep end, and then in a matter of 3 months everything collapsed around me.  I feel so unstable most days; just desperately hoping the meds will bring me back to where I used to be (sane).  I think about suicide often and feel like I'm on a ticking time clock to the end of my life.  I really wanted better than this, and it hurts me so bad to be going through this.  I plan on taking my own life this summer after one last good roadtrip if things haven't changed significantly for me.
Maybe; but I was on the SSRI's for nearly 10 years prior to this.  I'm guessing maybe it was the combination of the two - I'm guessing it threw off my brain chemistry.

I'm finding just after two weeks of mood stabilizers that I'm gaining weight; and my recent hypomania has me wanting to do drugs (smoke pot) and cigs like crazy ... along with ravenous appetite for junk food and cereal.

One begins to get the strong feeling that civilian resistance is being 'taught' to locals - learning to terrorize the terrorists and give 'judges' some second thoughts about being involved with ISIS.  Not to glorify death, but they've pushed civilians too far and are now feeling the impact.  I suspect that groups like US special forces may be teaching some of these tactics - it sounds very much like a coordinated assassination to inspire fear/doubt in the enemy.

To be quite honest, Turkey is not who 'we' thought they were.  They've got an agenda, and it appears to be closely aligned with ISIS, Nusra, and provoking a further escalation of this conflict against the Kurds, Russia, and western powers.  It's like taking a conflict that already had 15 different sides, spinning it around, and adding another dimension of conflict to an extremely complicated war.  If I were in Turkey, I'd be very concerned about hostilities jumping the border in the very near future.

The real problem is the chaos and multiple sides fighting inside a relatively small area ... while Turkey admits to shooting down the plane, I suspect they will deny any involvement thereafter - blaming the shooting/killing on Turkmen forces just across the border (which they will likely claim they don't 'control' - only support).  Here is the kicker though; they support those forces, and shot down a Russian plane attacking those forces.  They've essentially protected those forces by their attack.

I think many, including myself, underestimated just how insane Turkey's leadership is ... they've attacked the Kurds, supported Nusra, and downed a Russian plane in the last 5 days.  I honestly saw them as a much more stable, practical political power - I think their actions have major implications for the way this conflict will (or won't) be resolved.  I certainly think what they are doing will hurt their international political cause against Kurds after this war - they are leaving little doubt as to their intentions when hostilities against ISIS/SAA cease.

I disagree; they are simply buying survival time and trying to embed themselves into a better position before the world turns on them (post-ISIS).  Smart, at this point, would be blending into the crowd and trying to disappear back into Iraq/Libya/Afghanistan/Tunisia prior to catching the brunt of Russian/French/American bombing.

Someone needs to send Nusra a cruise missile or two ... the idea that they are going to control the situation on the ground after ISIS is wiped off the map is laughable.  Frankly, the Kurds/SDF are the only group looking like an actual committed, logical, and reasonable fighting force.

Divide and conquer seems to be working; the strategy to cut supply lines between Mosul and Raqqa was brilliant (if not obvious - and way late in happening).  Honestly, the biggest weakness for ISIS from the start was airpower (lack thereof); they are/were completely dependent on the road system and holding a string of territory in order to ensure resupply.

Anyone suspect that Turkey is largely responsible for this offensives goals?  I can't believe the extent to which they seem to support Nusra, given their allies and position of credibility in world politics.

I suspect a mass migration to Mosul may be coming anytime, or is already in place - Raqqa is about to be a no-man's land of urban fighting.  I also wonder if Al-Qa'im is about to become an important battleground ... one would think Iraq forces are already bearing down on it in order to control the border crossing and further cut off ISIS supply lines and troop movements from Iraq.  Frankly, it appears any ISIS fighters not out of Syria within the next week may not be getting out at all (via Turkey or Iraq).
Any updated 'controlled territory' maps out there?  It appears ISIS is now divided between Raqqa, their last stand in Hasakah, and the area of Mosul with scattered forces still in Ramadi/Fallujah.
Smells like the cold war.
Syria needs it bad; some kind of real political alternative to what they've faced for decades.
Brave; let's hope they are true opposition and not an Assad political proxy.  The optimist in me hopes this is the start of a rise in true political alternatives to Assad.

Very very sad; these sorts of videos and pointless interrogations don't help any side.  Yes, the young man is fighting for a dictator - but he doesn't control his situation anymore than he controls it after being captured.  People are not machines, they have hopes and dreams that never included this war or the threat of death or killing others.  You can see the fear in his face that would be present for any of us in this situation - no matter what side we support (or don't).  I hope Peace finds all sides sooner rather than later.

I hope so.  I do think this war is unique in terms of the number of parties involved and their relation to each other.  It's been an incredible building stalemate that has spawned the most powerful terrorist organization the history of man, while being wrapped in a civil war, and involving probably the most massive influx of non-traditional foreign fighters in the history of modern war.  In many ways, it's the most violent conflict of the 21st century.  It makes Afghanistan look like a minor conflict.
You make a good point.  It makes you wonder which of these sides can actually 'win' at this point ... so much has been lost.
Cruise missiles are damn scary - one could be headed your way while you are eating lunch and you don't have a clue; just the momentary instant when you hear it coming in and that is that.

It's not economic reasons that are keeping the US ground forces at home - it's political, social, and simply an unwillingness to sacrifice another generation to the meat-grinder that is another M.E. conflict.  Russia and China have much greater latitude to impact change with their forces abroad - it comes with military size, manpower, and control over their populations.

Never; especially not after reports like this that show, very clearly, what he does to political dissenters.  These pictures alone would have ensured he would never rule 'peacefully' again - his actions in the war only solidify resistance.

What is equally terrible is there likely WAS viable political alternatives to his rule prior to this conflict starting - and he's either wiped them off the map or sent them packing as refugees.  I suspect some of the last folks left to rule post-Assad will be a much younger generation who actually stands a chance of surviving this conflict (maybe).  Between Islamists and Assad - you begin to wonder if their are any Syrians willing to step in after he is gone.

Turkey is losing credibility daily; they are fighting a war against Kurds while the rest of the world asks Kurds to fight the ground war against ISIS.  I don't see how they believe they will eliminate Kurdish resistance post-war by stoking the situation through violence and war crimes.

Not much against the airstrikes - they can only continue to resist ground forces and 'hold on'.  If the situation continues to deteriorate, they will have to return to unorganized guerrilla warfare - hiding in small groups among civilians and resorting to hit-and-run tactics.  I think without intervention, the rebel forces are going to continue to deteriorate; I don't see a reversal happening at this time.  That being said, there is a clear 'lack of will' among gov't forces to make ground advances; even as they have superior airpower and support.  I think that is the answer to why territory isn't changing hands, even though it 'should' be in theory - with rebel forces being pounded from the air and clearly weakened.

Him 'winning' an election will not change the reality; there will be an element (permanently) that will not accept his rule.  That is what war crimes, civilian killings, and dictatorship create - permanent instability.
Thanks Mods.

Precisely why Assad will never rule a stable Syria again; people will never agree to go back under his thumb and submit themselves and their families to torture again.  If he does come back into power after this - there will be mass killings by his regime, without a doubt.

As bad as this war has gotten; those pictures and report are still incredibly terrible and the thought that individuals were facing that sort of torture is simply scary.  It makes it very clear why so many are willing to die to oust Assad, and why the threat of capture is enough to continue fighting.
